hints: Picture a single chromosome in prophase. It is not a thin single thread now, it is the fat X-shape after DNA replication in S phase. How many chromatids share one centromere?
Remember each chromatid is one DNA double helix (2 polynucleotide strands) with 2 ends. So double everything per chromatid except the shared centromere.
walkthrough:
**Recall what prophase means**

Great start. Prophase of mitosis comes after interphase, so S phase has already happened.

That means DNA replication is complete and each chromosome is now made of two identical sister chromatids joined together.

**Count centromeres and chromatids**

Think of one X-shaped chromosome as one unit.

It has 2 sister chromatids held together at 1 shared centromere. So centromeres = 1, chromatids = 2.

**Count polynucleotide strands and telomeres**

Now zoom in. Each chromatid is one DNA molecule, and one DNA molecule is a double helix.

That is 2 polynucleotide strands per chromatid:
$$2 \text{ chromatids} \times 2 \text{ strands} = 4 \text{ strands}$$

Each chromatid also has 2 ends, and each end has a telomere:
$$2 \text{ chromatids} \times 2 \text{ telomeres} = 4 \text{ telomeres}$$

**Match to the row**

So we need 1 centromere, 2 chromatids, 4 polynucleotide strands, 4 telomeres.

That is exactly row B.

options.A: Describes an unreplicated chromosome (as in G1) with 2 strands and 2 telomeres, but in prophase replication has already given 2 chromatids, 4 strands and 4 telomeres.
options.B: Correct. One replicated chromosome in prophase has 1 shared centromere, 2 sister chromatids, 4 polynucleotide strands (2 per DNA molecule) and 4 telomeres (2 per chromatid).
options.C: Wrong because a single chromosome has only 1 centromere holding the sisters together, and it clearly has 2 chromatids in prophase, not 0.
options.D: Wrong because it gives 2 centromeres (that would be two separate chromosomes) and only 2 strands, but two chromatids must contain 4 strands in total.
